headline: GDX TURNS 20: Record Miner Cash Flows at Lowest P/E in 40 Quarters — VanEck Says Rally Is 'Early Innings'
snippet: VanEck's Imaru Casanova marks GDX's 20th anniversary (launched May 16, 2006) by noting gold miners are generating record cash flows while trading at a 20.2x trailing P/E — the lowest level in at least 40 quarters of consistent data. With GDX up 108% year-over-year and top holdings like Newmont, Agnico Eagle, and Barrick printing exceptional earnings, Casanova argues the miners-to-metal outperformance cycle is only beginning.

headline: GOLD BOUNCES to $4,570; SILVER Recovers 2% After Week-Long CPI Beatdown Erased Rate-Cut Hopes
snippet: Gold spot climbed $30.60 (+0.67%) to $4,570.50 and silver rose 2.1% to $77.54 on May 18 as the U.S. dollar softened and physical premiums held firm in Shanghai and Mumbai. The recovery follows a brutal week: April CPI printed 3.8% — above forecast — silver crashed 7% to $76, and markets fully priced out any 2026 Fed rate cuts. The gold-to-silver ratio sits at 58.9:1 as both metals try to stabilize.

headline: ZAMBIA Forms State Gold JV to Formalize Artisanal Mining and Build In-Country Processing
snippet: Zambia's state investment firm ZCCM-IH has teamed with Mining Mineral Resources to launch Kyalo Goldfields Ltd., holding a 51% controlling stake in a new gold exploration and processing venture in North-Western Province. The JV targets the formalization of chaotic artisanal mining activity from last year's gold rush while building downstream processing capacity to retain more value inside Zambia's borders.

headline: EQUINOX + ORLA Merge: US$18.5 Billion Deal Creates New North American Senior Gold Producer
snippet: Equinox Gold and Orla Mining announced an all-share combination creating a new senior North American gold producer with an US$18.5 billion implied market cap and 1.1 million oz of expected 2026 production, anchored by three Canadian cornerstone assets: Greenstone (ON), Valentine (NL), and Musselwhite (ON). Orla shareholders receive 1.00 Equinox share per share held; the deal targets a Q3 2026 close with a funded growth path to 1.9 million oz.

headline: Elemental Royalty Buys VIZSLA ROYALTIES for C$327M, Locks In 3.5% NSR on High-Grade Panuco Silver-Gold
snippet: Elemental Royalty Corp. will acquire Vizsla Royalties Corp. in a C$327 million (US$239 million) all-cash-or-share arrangement at a 31% premium, securing 2%–3.5% NSR royalties on the Panuco silver-gold project in Sinaloa, Mexico — a deposit projected to produce 17.4 million silver-equivalent ounces annually over its initial mine life. The deal accelerates Elemental's consolidation of the royalty and streaming space.

headline: NGEx DRILLS 17m at 207g/t Au at Lunahuasi — Including 2m at 1,740g/t — Phase 4 Program Now Complete
snippet: NGEx Minerals' Phase 4 program at the 100%-owned Lunahuasi copper-gold-silver project in San Juan, Argentina returned a highlight of 17.3 metres at 207.79 g/t gold, 2.02% copper, and 16.2 g/t silver from 335 metres depth — including a 2-metre interval at 1,740 g/t gold. Two ultra-high-grade gold zones lying 660 metres apart confirm the bonanza gold component extends across the full deposit footprint. Results from 12 remaining holes are pending.

headline: HEMLO Mining Discovers South-Rim Zone: 16.1 g/t Au Over 8.1m Beside Active Ontario C-Zone Mining
snippet: Hemlo Mining Corp. (TSXV: HMMC) intercepted 16.07 g/t gold over 8.1 metres — including 2 metres at 59.7 g/t — in a newly reinterpreted South-Rim Zone at the historic Hemlo Gold Mine near Marathon, Ontario. All seven initial holes of the 20-hole program hit mineralization, with the plunge-controlled structure mapped as open over more than 1.5 km vertically within a 300-metre east-west corridor adjacent to the active C-Zone.

headline: COPPER HIT $14,000/t on LME Then Retreated as Hot CPI Data Raised Rate-Hike Odds
snippet: LME copper breached $14,000 per tonne on May 12 — within reach of the all-time high — before retreating nearly 5% as April's surprise 3.8% U.S. CPI print reinforced the case for no Fed rate cuts in 2026 and drove profit-taking across industrial metals. Copper remains 37% above year-ago levels, underpinned by AI data centre buildouts and grid modernization, but the hawkish rate backdrop is a near-term headwind.

headline: Premier American Uranium FIRES UP 100,000 ft Kaycee ISR Drill Program in Wyoming's Powder River Basin
snippet: Premier American Uranium (TSXV: PYR) launched a 100,000-foot ISR drill campaign at its Kaycee project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin on May 5, targeting approximately 33,000 ft of step-out drilling at Outpost and 51,000 ft at Rustler — both roll-front uranium targets with encouraging 2025 intersections. The program aims to infill between known mineralized zones and delineate subsurface host channels ahead of a resource update.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE Hits CNY 175,000/t in China — Up 50% YTD — as Battery Storage and EV Demand Collide
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate in China crossed CNY 175,000 per tonne in May — a 50% year-to-date gain — driven by Chinese VAT rebate cuts on lithium-ion batteries effective April 1, surging data centre energy storage demand, and front-loaded EV production. Spodumene concentrate is up nearly 30% over the same period. Battery-grade lithium carbonate has roughly doubled since Q4 2025 to US$26,278 per tonne globally; analysts warn speculative buying has moved prices ahead of fundamentals.

headline: SILVER at $77: Stop Chasing the Price Target — Why Position Sizing Matters More Right Now
snippet: With silver having briefly surged to $87 on US-China tariff relief before crashing back to $76 on the April CPI shock, GoldSilver.com argues retail investors keep making the same mistake: fixating on a price target instead of managing position size through high-volatility windows. The piece lays out a practical framework for accumulating silver exposure during drawdowns rather than chasing momentum at recent highs.

headline: INDIA and RUSSIA Near Critical Minerals Deal on Lithium and Rare Earths to Reduce China Dependence
snippet: India's Ministry of Mines and Russian counterparts have shared a draft preliminary agreement covering critical mineral exploration, processing, and technology transfer — with a primary focus on lithium and rare earth elements. A formal signing is expected within roughly two months, making this one of the more consequential non-Western supply-chain diversification moves since China began imposing critical mineral export restrictions.
